title: Solo devx morning sprint log
content:
Morning quick log — aim: 3 tiny wins before lunch. Tone: fast, noisy, scribbly.

09:10 - quick mental map
- unblock sample-app parity with hosted API (streaming + errors)
- reproduce tutorial step where KV cache example breaks on long context
- patch docs to mention recommended batch_size defaults for Llama-3-70B variants

Immediate todos (priority order)
1) surface deterministic example for stream->file fallback in sample-app (30–45m)
   - problem: current sample shows streaming only; if stream fails we silently return partial output. user reports lost assistant response.
   - quick patch: add `on_stream_error` hook and small snippet showing file-write fallback + retry with shorter max_tokens.
   - linked PR: gh#8112 (WIP) — need unit test that fakes aborted chunk.

2) KV cache tutorial repro notes (60–90m)
   - repro steps: follow tutorial-05-kv-cache.md, run sample playbook with sequence length 8k, set cache_enabled=true. Observed: repeated tokens after warmup (~step 14).
   - hypothesis: we append cache prefill twice when sequence crosses chunk boundary. Could be sample-app's `merge_prefixes` helper bug.
   - quick instrument: add logs `KV PREFILL: start/end` + timestamp and dump `cache_keys.length` at each attention step.
   - test dataset: use toy-dialogue-2.json (small, shares context patterns that trigger bug)

3) Doc gap: batching guidance for SDK `generate` API (15–20m)
   - users confuse `batch_size` vs `concurrency_limit` — need one-paragraph explanation and a table of recommended starting values by model family and hardware tier.
   - add tip: "if latency SLOs <300ms, keep batch_size<=4 and use concurrency_limit=2 on shared-hosted"

Daily micro-log / experiments (notes):
- Experiment A: lower `batch_size` in sample-app to 2 and re-run load harness on local convex (2x A100) — saw tail latency drop ~18% but throughput lost ~22% (expected). Make a note in optimize checklist.
- Experiment B: try quantized llama-3-70B-int8 on a single V100: crashes in `kernel_select` path (segfault). Add stacktrace to GH issue and ping infra (@Evelyn).

Small copy edits to push after lunch:
- tutorial-02-getting-started: clarify env var names (REDWOOD_API_KEY vs REDWOOD_KEY) — remove contradictory examples- sample-app README: show minimal config for streaming fallback

Blocking things to follow up:
- Need unit test harness that can simulate partial stream delivery (network abort). Related ticket: INF-3421. If Maya can help mock the socket, we can add test in `streaming_test.ts`.
- Patch to `merge_prefixes` might be risky; prefer an instrumentation-only PR first so we can capture root cause on customer repro.

Random quick reference snippets (copy into PR later):
- on_stream_error example (pseudo):
  ``
  client.generateStream(req, {
    onData(chunk) { writeToStream(chunk) },
    onError(err) { writeToFile(recoveryPath); client.generateSync(retryReq) }
  })
  ``

- kv cache diagnostic (pseudo):
  ``
  if (cache) {
    console.log('KV PREFILL', step, cache.keys().length);
  }
  ``

Mini retro notes — what worked
- keeping one tiny goal list helped ship small PRs instead of big vague ones.
- pair-debugging with Maya yesterday made the KV cache instrumentation much faster.

Next steps (this afternoon)
- finish PR for streaming fallback sample (assign reviewers: Maya, Evelyn)
- add instrumentation to sample-app KV path (submit as non-breaking log-only PR)
- write a short "batching primer" doc and link it from SDK README
- drop 30m in calendar for cross-team sync if we hit a customer repro

Questions / unresolved
- Is there a strong preference for `concurrency_limit` naming across SDK languages? (JS currently `concurrencyLimit`, Python `max_concurrency`) — should we standardize? — ask @docs-owners.
- For the kv cache duplication, do we have any long-running traces stored from demos that reproduce (maybe `/devx/demos/2026-02-18`)? If so, request archival copy.

Tiny wins checklist (tick when done):
- [ ] streaming fallback snippet pushed to GH
- [ ] kv cache logs added to sample-app
- [ ] one-paragraph batching guidance written
- [ ] open a follow-up ticket for naming standardization

Notes to self: keep PRs tiny, prefer observable-first patches, and write one-sentence changelog entries for customer-facing docs.

End of morning sprint log. Will update after lunch with PR numbers and outcomes.
